newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 20.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.

- The next Irish government should tighten Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn's budget plans for 1998 and 1999, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) suggests in a major analysis of Ireland's economy.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton and the leader of the main opposition party, Bertie Ahern, will risk everything in a head-to-head television showdown on June 4.
- Irish police are to get new powers to hold suspects for questioning on serious crimes for 36 hours longer than the current average length of time.
- A sharp increase in tea and coffee prices is expected to hit Irish shops and cafes.
- Information overload is leading to greater stress levels in Irish business, according to a new survey.

- Ireland's Aer Rianta is to become the world's second largest operator of duty-free shops following confirmation that it had been selected to manage 12 tobacco and alcohol outlets at Hong Kong's giant new airport for an initial five-year period.

- Ireland's Prime Minister John Bruton intends to do nothing about abortion if his government is re-elected on June 6. - Well over 100 Irish pounds of weekly income would be exempted entirely from tax under plans to be put forward in manifestos from two of Ireland's three government parties, Labour and the Democratic Left.

- As campaigning enters its last day both Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army, and the fringe "loyalist" parties predict they will secure strong support in Wednesday's local elections in Northern Ireland.
- An OECD survey forecasts a continuing rapid expansion of the Irish economy.
- Irish police in riot gear stormed a house in County Cork, in the south of Ireland, on Monday and overpowered a man armed with knives who had threatened his family and neighbours.

- Old-age pensioners must be granted freedom to hold 20,000 Irish pounds in savings before losing the right to any social benefits or pensions, the Labour Party will demand in any post-election programme for government talks.
